newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cabinet sets four pct rise in minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: French cabinet sets four pct rise in minimum wage.

text.p: The French cabinet on Wednesday formally agreed a four percent increase in France's national minimum wage, Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said.
The rise "represents a three percent increase in purchasing power because inflation has been less than one percent," Strauss-Kahn told reporters after the weekly cabinet talks.

The increase in the so-called SMIC, which stands at 6,406.79 francs a month, or just under 38 francs an hour, was first announced to parliament by new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin last week.

Economists said then that the rise was surprisingly low and sent a political message that despite demands from the left wing of the Socialist-led coalition, rapid wage increases might have to wait until job creation grew more robust.
Communists and unions had pushed for a much bigger increase, of as much as eight percent, this year.
Jospin said in his June 19 policy speech to the National Assembly that the four percent increase would be the biggest boost in purchasing power in 15 years for the low-paid.
About two million workers currently earn the minimum wage.
